citeAs: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911.
creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (Google, Yale University)
description: IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark for large language models focused on "verifiable instructions" — instructions whose compliance can be objectively and automatically verified (e.g., "write in more than 400 words", "mention the keyword AI at least 3 times"). It consists of 25 types of verifiable instructions and around 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions, enabling fully automatic assessment of instruction-following ability.
name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Prompts were manually checked and edited one by one after automated generation and rephrasing steps. Verifiable instructions were selected because they are either easy to verify or common in real-world applications. Each verifiable instruction has multiple variants in terms of parameters and phrasing.
rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that human evaluations are biased and inconsistent, and that model-based evaluations are potentially biased or limited by the evaluator LLM. IFEval is designed to mitigate these biases by focusing on objectively verifiable instructions. The authors note that very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically — edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed.
rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a four-step process: (1) generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; (2) using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts; (3) applying another few-shot prompting approach to rephrase each prompt to increase phrasing diversity; and (4) manually checking and editing each rephrased prompt one by one.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts were generated by concatenating a base prompt (e.g., "write an essay") with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions from a predefined list of 25 instruction types appended to the end.
rai:dataLimitations: The current implementation can be improved by: (1) increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions; (2) extending to multi-modal use cases. The loose criterion for instruction-following verification, while reducing false negatives, may introduce false positives. Not all instructions are 100% objectively and automatically verifiable — edge cases exist.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A loose accuracy metric is computed by applying eight transformations to model responses (removing markdown font modifiers such as * and **, removing the first line, removing the last line, and combinations thereof) to reduce false negatives in instruction-following verification.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Generated prompts were filtered using few-shot prompting to remove illogical prompts (e.g., conflicting instructions such as limiting paragraphs to 5 while also requiring fewer than 20 words). Remaining prompts were rephrased using few-shot prompting to increase diversity, then manually reviewed and edited.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Ensuring that LLMs can consistently adhere to given directives is paramount for safety and reliability. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems. IFEval provides a standardized, reproducible benchmark to help address these safety concerns.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models (LLMs) in a fully automatic, objective, and reproducible manner. The benchmark enables researchers to identify which types of instructions LLMs fail to follow and to compare different LLMs across various instruction categories.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting (using a large language model) was used to identify and remove illogical prompts, and to rephrase prompts for diversity. Deterministic programs are used to verify whether model responses follow each verifiable instruction.

null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset consists of prompts with verifiable instructions verified programmatically; no per-item human annotation count is described.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No annotator demographics are described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality analysis is reported; verification is programmatic.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No external annotation platform is mentioned; prompts were created and curated internally.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No explicit data collection timeframe is stated for the prompts (model responses were scraped in November and August 2023, but that is evaluation, not dataset collection).
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described; future work mentions expanding instructions but no formal plan.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is collected; the dataset consists of synthetic prompts.
